subject: general
question: Lok Adalats aim to settle disputes amicably by promoting which type of resolution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amicable/compromise**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lok Adalats** are alternative dispute resolution forums in India established under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**. They focus on resolving disputes outside formal judicial proceedings.
 
• The primary aim of Lok Adalats is to promote **amicable settlement** of disputes through mutual understanding and compromise between the parties involved.
 
• Disputes resolved through Lok Adalats include cases related to **civil matters, family disputes, bank recovery cases, motor vehicle accident claims, and other compoundable criminal offences.**
 
• Lok Adalats ensure that justice is delivered **quickly, without incurring significant expenses**, and with minimal procedural complexities.
 
• The awards passed by Lok Adalats are legally binding and hold the status of a civil court decree, ensuring compliance by both parties. **Appeals cannot be filed against the decisions of Lok Adalats.**
 
• The concept of Lok Adalats is rooted in the philosophy of **Gandhian principles** of resolving disputes through peaceful negotiations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987:**

 
 
• This act provides statutory backing to Lok Adalats and ensures free legal aid to economically weaker sections of society.
 
• Under Section 19 of the Act, Lok Adalats are organized at different levels—state, district, taluk, or village.
 
• The Act promotes access to justice for all, especially marginalized sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Features of Lok Adalats:**
 
 
• Lok Adalats operate with minimal procedural formalities, enabling swift resolution of disputes.
 
• It ensures a **win-win situation**, as settlements are made with the consent of both parties.
 
• There is no court fee involved, making it cost-effective for litigants.
 
• Matters resolved in Lok Adalats cannot be reopened in any court, ensuring finality of decisions.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Lok Adalats:**
 
 
• Encourages **peaceful coexistence** by promoting compromise rather than confrontation.
 
• Reduces the burden on formal courts and contributes to faster disposal of cases.
 
• Ensures **access to justice** for rural and economically weaker sections.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Cases Resolved:**
 
 
• Motor vehicle accident compensation cases settled amicably between the claimant and insurance companies.
 
• Family disputes resolved through mutual agreement, avoiding lengthy legal battles.
 
• Bank recovery cases where borrowers and banks negotiate repayment terms.
 
• Compoundable criminal cases resolved through compromise between parties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:** Lok Adalats derive their concept from ancient Indian traditions of panchayats, where disputes were resolved within the community through mediation and compromise.
 
• **Role of National Legal Services Authority (NALSA):** NALSA coordinates Lok Adalats across India and provides guidelines for their functioning.
 
• **Recent Developments:** Lok Adalats have increasingly adopted technology to conduct virtual hearings, ensuring accessibility even during times like the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• **Global Perspective:** Alternative dispute resolution mechanisms like Lok Adalats align with international practices promoting out-of-court settlements, such as arbitration and mediation.
